newsitem.title: UK: BP wins injunction against Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: BP wins injunction against Greenpeace.

text.p: British Petroleum won a court injunction on Tuesday banning environmental group Greenpeace from disrupting the company's search for oil in the Foinaven field in the north Atlantic.
BP also launched a lawsuit against Greenpeace claiming 1.23 million pounds ($2.1 million) in damages for the disruption to its operations already caused by the group.

But the oil giant said later on Tuesday that it was willing to suspend its damages claim provided Greenpeace agreed not to hinder BP's oil exploration and production in the Atlantic Frontier area any further.
The interim interdict was granted by Edinburgh's Court of Sessions following an eight-day protest by Greenpeace members who boarded the Stena Dee floating oil platform.
The platform was headed from Norway to the Foinaven field some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland.
The protest, which ended on Sunday after Greenpeace said it could no longer guarantee protesters' safety, was aimed at halting oil exploration in the area.
The court order also applied to two Greenpeace employees, Sarah Burton and Chris Rose, and the master of its campaigning ship, Jon Castle.
Greenpeace said the claim for damages could bankrupt its operations in Britain.
But BP said in a statement: "BP's principal concern is not the recovery of damages. Rather, it is to ensure that its lawful operations are not interfered with and that safety is not compromised."
Four protesters were each fined 200 pounds in a Scottish court on Monday after pleading guilty to breaching the peace.
Greenpeace appealed for public support in its court battle against BP.

"BP made 1.5 billion pounds profit in the first six months of the year -- it makes more in profit in 48 hours than Greenpeace receives in income in a year," Greenpeace deputy executive director Chris Rose said in a statement.

Greenpeace campaigners have also been blocking an Alantic Richfield Co rig off the Alaskan coast to keep it away from a field in the Arctic Beaufort Sea. A U.S. federal judge on Friday ordered the activists to stay outside a moving safety buffer around the mobile rig.
The blockades, which Greenpeace says are intended to fight global warming, are part of its most ambitious campaign yet against the oil industry. It calls for a switch to renewable resources.
